recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-34278 unless the work group separately chooses to revisit whether conditional PATCH should be stronger than SHOULD.
issue_request: FHIR-34278 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for the FHIR-core HTTP page. It asked whether the PATCH section incorrectly made PATCH mandatory for all servers and requested clarification plus correction of the Binary PATCH note typo from "not" to "note". The accepted resolution required servers that support PATCH to support the concurrency/resource-contention mechanism rather than requiring all servers to support conditional PATCH.
initial_application: The substantive wording change was applied by git commit 4bbadac472f4adf87cc53aedf5b5736652b39fa3, which replaced "servers SHALL support conditional PATCH" with wording requiring servers that support PATCH to support Concurrency Management. The typo called out by the issue is already corrected in current history by git commit 021fdd52eec1b71a39014469ed6df9dbb3804995, changing "not about PATCH on Binary" to "note about PATCH on Binary".
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes for 2022-03-14 record that the proposal made sense and was accepted as Persuasive with Modification by a 12-0-1 vote. Later HTTP-page editorial changes, including FHIR-39135 and FHIR-40957, refactored nearby wording from operations to interactions and renamed the linked concurrency section to Resource Contention without reversing the FHIR-34278 requirement scope. The active source/http.html page is linked from source/documentation.html as the RESTful API (HTTP) page.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/http.html already says servers that support PATCH SHALL support Resource Contention on the PATCH interaction, keeps conditional patch as a SHOULD where PATCH and Conditional Update are both supported, and uses the corrected "note about PATCH on Binary" text.

related_jiras.note: Later editorial restructuring touched source/http.html and moved the PATCH text without reversing the FHIR-34278 decision.
Later terminology cleanup changed nearby wording from operation to interaction and renamed the linked section to Resource Contention while preserving the requirement scope.
